user_input: Since this morning customers can't add anything to their cart: POST /cart/items returns 500, but viewing existing carts still works. CartService logs say 'OOM command not allowed'. The Redis memory graph has been climbing steadily for about two weeks, since we refactored the cart storage code. What is going on and how do we fix it safely?
ground_truth_diagnosis: CartService's Redis instance (CartCache) is full: it is capped at 2048 MB with the noeviction policy, so it rejects writes while reads still succeed. The steady growth since the refactor matches the documented cause of cart keys losing their TTL (SET instead of SETEX), so abandoned carts are never removed.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: CartCache is capped at 2048 MB and uses noeviction, which rejects writes but still serves reads.
CartService depends synchronously on CartCache.
A refactor that replaced SETEX with SET leaves cart keys without expiry, so memory grows over days to weeks.

user_input: Customers are receiving the same order confirmation email three or four times, and lag on the notification-service consumer group keeps growing. The group seems to rebalance every few minutes. The email provider's status page shows degraded latency today. Why is this happening?
ground_truth_diagnosis: The slow email provider makes NotificationService exceed the Kafka poll interval while processing a batch, so consumers are repeatedly removed from the group and their batches are reprocessed after each rebalance. Because emails are sent before offsets are committed and there is no idempotency check, every reprocessed batch sends the same emails again.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: NotificationService consumes order events from Kafka.
Batches that take longer than max.poll.interval.ms cause the consumer to be kicked out and the group to rebalance repeatedly.
Emails are sent before offsets are committed without an idempotency check, so reprocessed batches send duplicates.
